items.title: Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Summary - December 2, 2025
Board of Health Update
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner, provided an update on the current state of influenza, COVID-19 virus, and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). She cautioned that it is likely that the spread of these viruses will peak in the next month due to colder weather and holidays which result in extended close proximity interactions indoors. She recommended that individuals that are able to be vaccinated do so to limit the spread of viruses and protect the most vulnerable in the community.

She also noted that the Public Board of Health dashboard update will be delayed by one business day.

notes:
C. James provided a brief overview of the motion and highlighted the importance of access to affordable childcare with emphasis on the need for funding from the province.

Council discussed the motion and N. Salonen provided an amendment to add emphasis on rural centres which had unanimous consent.

items.title: Other Business
notes:
Responding to Council, Tim Brubacher, Regional Clerk/Director of Council and Administrative Services, confirmed that staff amend the procedural by-law before every new term of Council and have an ongoing list of amendments that will be presented to Council which will include a procedure to address if there is an error in voting during Council and Committee meetings.

In response to Council, W. Steffler confirmed that Waterloo Region Police Services capital projects are managed through the Region's request for proposal process, where applicable, and potentially could have a reduced cost from the budgeted amount.

motions.item_title: Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Summary - December 2, 2025
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo endorse Grand River Transit’s Ontario Transit Investment Fund application to introduce new and improved Township transit services as outlined in report TSD-TRS-25-009 dated December 2, 2025. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions regarding the property municipally known as 120 Victoria Street South in the City of Kitchener, as described in Report PDL-GDS-25-015, dated December 2, 2025: Approve a joint Tax Increment Grant with the Regional amount not to exceed $656,291, to be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment; and Authorize the Region’s Commissioner of Planning, Development and Legislative Services and Commissioner, Corporate Services / Chief Financial Officer to execute any associated agreements, assignments, amendments or other related documents with the registered owner of 120 Victoria Street South in the City of Kitchener with the form and content of such Tax Increment Grant agreement(s), any subsequent assignments of the agreement, or other related documents to be satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions regarding the property municipally known as 108 Garment Street in the City of Kitchener, as described in Report PDL-GDS-25-016, dated December 2, 2025: Approve a joint Tax Increment Grant with the Regional amount not to exceed $745,641, to be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment; and Authorize the Region’s Commissioner of Planning, Development and Legislative Services and Commissioner, Corporate Services / Chief Financial Officer to execute any associated agreements, assignments, amendments or other related documents with the registered owner of 108 Garment Street in the City of Kitchener, with the form and content of such Tax Increment Grant agreement(s), any subsequent assignments of the agreement, or other related documents to be satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor. WHEREAS the implementation of Extended Producer Responsibility fully shifts responsibilities for recycling collection away from the Region of Waterloo, including decisions to reduce curbside recycling collection frequency; WHEREAS Regional staff intend to monitor changes to landfill volumes following implementation of Extended Producer Responsibility in 2026; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services and Commissioner of Resident Experience and Strategy: Engage with Circular Materials to incorporate curbside recycling collection information provided by Circular Materials in shared materials, where possible. Report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee in Q1 2027 with: Information regarding changes to the volume of waste being brought to Regional landfill following the March 2026 transition; A summary of the volume and nature of resident inquiries received by the Region regarding curbside recycling collection following the January 1, 2026 transition.
motions.text_html:
1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo endorse Grand River Transit’s Ontario Transit Investment Fund application to introduce new and improved Township transit services as outlined in report TSD-TRS-25-009 dated December 2, 2025.
  2. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions regarding the property municipally known as 120 Victoria Street South in the City of Kitchener, as described in Report PDL-GDS-25-015, dated December 2, 2025:
    1. Approve a joint Tax Increment Grant with the Regional amount not to exceed $656,291, to be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment; and
    2. Authorize the Region’s Commissioner of Planning, Development and Legislative Services and Commissioner, Corporate Services / Chief Financial Officer to execute any associated agreements, assignments, amendments or other related documents with the registered owner of 120 Victoria Street South in the City of Kitchener with the form and content of such Tax Increment Grant agreement(s), any subsequent assignments of the agreement, or other related documents to be satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor.
  3. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions regarding the property municipally known as 108 Garment Street in the City of Kitchener, as described in Report PDL-GDS-25-016, dated December 2, 2025:
    1. Approve a joint Tax Increment Grant with the Regional amount not to exceed $745,641, to be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment; and
    2. Authorize the Region’s Commissioner of Planning, Development and Legislative Services and Commissioner, Corporate Services / Chief Financial Officer to execute any associated agreements, assignments, amendments or other related documents with the registered owner of 108 Garment Street in the City of Kitchener, with the form and content of such Tax Increment Grant agreement(s), any subsequent assignments of the agreement, or other related documents to be satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor.
  4. WHEREAS the implementation of Extended Producer Responsibility fully shifts responsibilities for recycling collection away from the Region of Waterloo, including decisions to reduce curbside recycling collection frequency;
    WHEREAS Regional staff intend to monitor changes to landfill volumes following implementation of Extended Producer Responsibility in 2026; 
    THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Commissioner of Engineering and Environmental Services and Commissioner of Resident Experience and Strategy:
    1. Engage with Circular Materials to incorporate curbside recycling collection information provided by Circular Materials in shared materials, where possible.
    2. Report to the Sustainability, Infrastructure, and Development Committee in Q1 2027 with:
      1. Information regarding changes to the volume of waste being brought to Regional landfill following the March 2026 transition;
      2. A summary of the volume and nature of resident inquiries received by the Region regarding curbside recycling collection following the January 1, 2026 transition.

motions.item_title: Councillor C. James, Re: Canada-Wide Early Learning Child Care Advocacy
motions.text: Whereas the Region of Waterloo, as the provincially designated Service System Manager for early learning and childcare, is responsible for planning, allocating, and managing licensed child care growth in accordance with provincial requirements; and Whereas demand for childcare significantly exceeds the supply of provincially funded spaces, with over 14,000 children currently on the waitlist, demonstrating a critical shortfall in affordable, high-quality childcare for families in our rapidly growing community; and Whereas notwithstanding the provincially funded junior kindergarten program, the provincial government’s contributions to the CWELCC program fall far short of the federal contribution despite this being a provincial responsibility. Whereas Waterloo Region is a unique and rapidly growing community projected to reach one million residents , and this growth includes infants, toddlers, and young children, yet planning and funding models often view growth predominantly through an adult lens, overlooking that children are essential contributors to the present and future health and vibrancy of our communities; and Whereas Waterloo Region has been underfunded by the Province of Ontario, creating limitations on the Region’s ability to support children, families, and operators, despite high need and sustained population growth; and Whereas childcare access is an equity issue, disproportionately impacting women who bear most caregiving responsibilities, limiting their participation in the workforce, contributing to the local affordability crisis, and affecting economic stability for families across Waterloo Region; and Whereas Whereas the provincial funding model does not provide sufficient local flexibility to respond to emerging needs and opportunities, even though this flexibility could allow operators to open additional spaces faster, and could allow operators to better support children with special needs and families eligible for fee subsidy; and Whereas several provinces and territories across Canada have already reached or are publicly reporting success in reaching regulated child-care fees of approximately $10-a-day or less under the Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) program, including Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, and the territories such as Nunavut and Yukon, while Quebec contributes approximately $2.76 billion annually to sustain its long-established $10-a-day child-care system, demonstrating that meaningful and sustained provincial investment is essential for affordability, access, stability, and long-term success in early learning and child care; and Whereas the Province of Ontario recently added $276 million in childcare funding, an amount that is not proportional to the scale of unmet need nor comparable to the level of federal investment that has enabled the CWELCC system; and Whereas interest in operating licensed childcare significantly exceeds the provincially funded growth allocation, with many qualified operators unable to receive approval due to insufficient provincial funding; and Whereas the Region of Waterloo’s childcare system operates with 99.6% utilization of CWELCC infant, toddler, and preschool spaces, illustrating a system at full capacity with no room to absorb further demand without enhanced provincial investment. Therefore Be It Resolved That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo: Formally advocate to the Province of Ontario and the Minister of Education for substantial additional CWELCC funding to address the Region’s rapidly growing population including the thousands of children who are part of this growth and to address the current waitlist of 14,000 children and persistent historic underfunding. Request the Province provide greater local flexibility in funding , to enable faster, more efficient growth, and to respond to demonstrated community needs, including for children with special needs and families eligible for fee subsidy. Call on the Province to match the level of commitment shown by the federal government , acknowledging that the recent $276 million provincial contribution is insufficient relative to both the need and the federal investment driving the CWELCC system. Emphasize that insufficient provincial investment worsens gender inequities , contributes to the affordability crisis facing families, and limits women’s economic participation contrary to the goals of a strong, inclusive provincial economy. Request that the Province recognize Waterloo Region’s unique pressures as a large, growing Region with rural and urban centres and provide targeted, needs-based funding to the region that reflects its demographic growth, labour market importance, and the current inequities in childcare access. Direct the Regional Chair to communicate this motion to: The Premier of Ontario; The Minister of Education; Local MPs; Local MPPs; The Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO); and The Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM).
motions.text_html:
Whereas the Region of Waterloo, as the provincially designated Service System Manager for early learning and childcare, is responsible for planning, allocating, and managing licensed child care growth in accordance with provincial requirements; and

Whereas demand for childcare significantly exceeds the supply of provincially funded spaces, with over 14,000 children currently on the waitlist, demonstrating a critical shortfall in affordable, high-quality childcare for families in our rapidly growing community; and

Whereas notwithstanding the provincially funded junior kindergarten program, the provincial government’s contributions to the CWELCC program fall far short of the federal contribution despite this being a provincial responsibility.

Whereas Waterloo Region is a unique and rapidly growing community projected to reach one million residents, and this growth includes infants, toddlers, and young children, yet planning and funding models often view growth predominantly through an adult lens, overlooking that children are essential contributors to the present and future health and vibrancy of our communities; and

Whereas Waterloo Region has been underfunded by the Province of Ontario, creating limitations on the Region’s ability to support children, families, and operators, despite high need and sustained population growth; and

Whereas childcare access is an equity issue, disproportionately impacting women who bear most caregiving responsibilities, limiting their participation in the workforce, contributing to the local affordability crisis, and affecting economic stability for families across Waterloo Region; and

Whereas Whereas the provincial funding model does not provide sufficient local flexibility to respond to emerging needs and opportunities, even though this flexibility could allow operators to open additional spaces faster, and could allow operators to better support children with special needs and families eligible for fee subsidy; and

Whereas several provinces and territories across Canada have already reached or are publicly reporting success in reaching regulated child-care fees of approximately $10-a-day or less under the Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) program, including Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, and the territories such as Nunavut and Yukon, while Quebec contributes approximately $2.76 billion annually to sustain its long-established $10-a-day child-care system, demonstrating that meaningful and sustained provincial investment is essential for affordability, access, stability, and long-term success in early learning and child care; and

Whereas the Province of Ontario recently added $276 million in childcare funding, an amount that is not proportional to the scale of unmet need nor comparable to the level of federal investment that has enabled the CWELCC system; and

Whereas interest in operating licensed childcare significantly exceeds the provincially funded growth allocation, with many qualified operators unable to receive approval due to insufficient provincial funding; and

Whereas the Region of Waterloo’s childcare system operates with 99.6% utilization of CWELCC infant, toddler, and preschool spaces, illustrating a system at full capacity with no room to absorb further demand without enhanced provincial investment.

Therefore Be It Resolved That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo:

Formally advocate to the Province of Ontario and the Minister of Education for substantial additional CWELCC funding to address the Region’s rapidly growing population including the thousands of children who are part of this growth and to address the current waitlist of 14,000 children and persistent historic underfunding.

Request the Province provide greater local flexibility in funding, to enable faster, more efficient growth, and to respond to demonstrated community needs, including for children with special needs and families eligible for fee subsidy.
Call on the Province to match the level of commitment shown by the federal government, acknowledging that the recent $276 million provincial contribution is insufficient relative to both the need and the federal investment driving the CWELCC system.

Emphasize that insufficient provincial investment worsens gender inequities, contributes to the affordability crisis facing families, and limits women’s economic participation contrary to the goals of a strong, inclusive provincial economy.

Request that the Province recognize Waterloo Region’s unique pressures as a large, growing Region with rural and urban centres and provide targeted, needs-based funding to the region that reflects its demographic growth, labour market importance, and the current inequities in childcare access.

Direct the Regional Chair to communicate this motion to:

  • The Premier of Ontario;
  • The Minister of Education;
  • Local MPs;
  • Local MPPs;
  • The Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO); and
  • The Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM).
